sections.h2: Ways to sell a Colleyville home
sections.html:
Cash buyers can close on whatever date suits you. A regular listing in a city of pricey houses usually takes longer but can pay more. Most Colleyville owners compare the two before deciding.

The city is in northeastern Tarrant County, and almost every household owns its home. Investor rentals are scarce here, and the typical house is large and has been in the family a long while.

  • Cash purchase: the buyer takes the house as it is, with no showings and no lender delays.
  • Listing: the right fit for a house in strong shape, with inspections and negotiated repairs.
  • Private sale: possible with a written contract and a title company handling the paperwork.

This is an affluent, settled city. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 25,727 people, 1.2% below the April 2020 base, living in 9,072 households of about 2.86 people each. Some 94.1% of residents kept the same address from the year before, so houses seldom come up for sale.

sections.h2: What to collect before you list
sections.html: Closing will call for a handful of papers, so find them now. You want your deed, the latest appraisal notice, proof of any homestead or over-65 exemption and a tax certificate. If the house was inherited, add the court order, executor's letters or recorded deed showing who may sign. Having everything on hand shortens the time between offer and closing.

The county tax office sends bills around October 1. January 31 is the last day before delinquency, and on February 1 penalty and interest begin. Penalty starts at 6 percent and rises monthly to 12 percent in July, while interest adds 1 percent each month.

On July 1, delinquent accounts go to tax attorneys, who can add up to 20 percent. Half-payment installments fall due November 30 and June 30. Older and disabled owners can use a quarterly plan that runs from January through July. At Tarrant Appraisal District, exemption filings close April 30 and protests May 15.

sections.h2: Filing a homestead exemption with Tarrant Appraisal District
sections.html:
There is no fee. Fill in the district's online form, or print form 50-114 and send it by mail or email. You will need a Texas driver's license or ID that shows the home address.

A buyer who moves in can claim the exemption starting from the move-in date, provided the earlier owner had none that year. The exemption also limits yearly appraisal growth to 10 percent, apart from new improvements and added land.

Heir property takes more paperwork: an ownership affidavit, the prior owner's death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation. Each other heir living in the house signs an authorization.

With a fifth of residents at 65 or older, many Colleyville owners hold a school tax ceiling. An extra school exemption of $60,000 applies at that age, and the ceiling can follow an owner to another Texas homestead. A surviving spouse who is 55 or older may keep it. Before you sell, ask the district whether your ceiling would transfer to the next home.

The title company divides the year's tax between buyer and seller. Because a lien attaches every January 1, the owner on that date remains liable for the year. When back taxes exist, the closing agent pays them from your proceeds. Order a tax certificate from the county before accepting any offer so you know the number.

sections.h2: Can heirs sell a Colleyville house quickly?
sections.html: Yes, once title is clear. A will may be probated up to four years after the owner's death. A small estate affidavit is limited to $75,000 excluding the homestead. Other routes include a muniment of title, an executor's deed, or a transfer on death deed recorded during the owner's lifetime. An heirship affidavit is only a sworn statement, and a buyer may refuse to rely on it.

Texas servicers generally wait until a loan is more than 120 days delinquent. The default notice leaves 20 days to reinstate, and the sale notice follows, with an auction at least 21 days later on a first Tuesday. If you close a sale first, the auction never happens.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or downsized house
sections.html:
With one resident in five aged 65 or more, many sales here follow a move to smaller quarters or a death in the family. Start by confirming who holds title and who has authority to sign. Next, gather the original will if there is one, a list of every heir and the recorded deed.

Then ask a title company what it will insure. Some will close on a court order alone. Others want a recorded transfer on death deed or an executor's deed. Settling this before you speak with buyers keeps an offer from stalling at the last minute.

The median owned home here is $784,900, and the median rent is $3,263. At that level, small differences in condition move the price a long way. A buyer financing the purchase will order an appraisal and an inspection, and either can reopen negotiation.

Gather receipts for roof, HVAC, foundation and plumbing work, plus any permits for additions. A written record of maintenance gives a buyer confidence and gives you something concrete to point to when an offer comes in low.

sections.h2: How a cash sale unfolds here
sections.html:
A cash buyer reviews the house, usually in a single visit, and sends a written offer. After you accept, the title company searches the records, collects payoff letters and prepares the deed. You pick a closing date and sign. In a city where large, long-held houses are common, expect the buyer to price in updates such as roofs, kitchens and systems, and expect the offer to land below a fully staged listing.

What you gain is certainty. No lender can pull back, no appraisal can come in short, and no showing schedule disrupts your household. For an owner moving out of state, settling an estate or avoiding months of carrying costs on a house worth $784,900, that certainty can be worth the discount. Compare written offers by the amount you would net.

faqs.q: Is selling without an agent common in Colleyville?
faqs.a: It can work for a house in sound condition if you can handle showings and paperwork. A title company still prepares the deed and splits the tax year.

faqs.q: When does a Colleyville buyer get the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: From the move-in date, when the seller had not claimed one that year.

faqs.q: Where is a Colleyville protest filed?
faqs.a: At Tarrant Appraisal District, by May 15 for the current year.

faqs.q: What if taxes on a Colleyville house are late?
faqs.a: Penalty climbs monthly to 12 percent in July and interest adds 1 percent monthly. Request the payoff amount from the county, and closing usually settles it.

faqs.q: Can an heir sign a Colleyville deed before probate ends?
faqs.a: Usually not. The buyer's title company wants a court order, an executor's authority or a recorded transfer on death deed.
